title: Parking a distance number puts your click at its centre, not at its edge
goal: Measuring a distance takes three clicks, and the third click parks the number. Click into the gap just under a button and half the number grows back up toward the button, because your click becomes the middle of the pill rather than the near edge of it. So the number ends up closer to the thing you measured than the spot you actually pointed at. Worth deciding whether the click should mean the near edge of the number instead.
notes: Found while fixing a-measurement-number-keeps-clear-of-the-edge-it. NOT a bug: the app obeys the click. The readout centres on labelAnchor, which is the head line, and the third click sets headOffset (CanvasMeasure.swift, measureHeadOffset). Evidence: Scripts/playtest/distance-three-clicks.json clicks [357, 840] to park the number on a button whose bottom edge is at y=816, i.e. 24 px of gap, and the pill (43 px tall) centres there, so it ends 2.5 px under the edge. That picture is queue/audits/2026-09-08-distance-three-clicks.png, the one that filed the clearance task. Size and Gap mode are unaffected: they place their own head and now stand off by half the pill height plus half the chip (MeasureBuilder.clearingHeadOffset). This is a UX judgement about what a click means, so it wants a decision card rather than a unilateral change.
acceptance: A decision card asks whether the third click means the centre of the number or its near edge, with a picture of each
Whichever way it goes, clicking a spot just off an element leaves the number where a person expected to put it
The existing distance walk still passes
